name: Damat documentation
description: Navigation map for the Damat docs site: the step-by-step guide plus every package's overview and internals.

topLevel.title: Overview
topLevel.summary: Top-level project overview and package index.

topLevel.title: The Damat Guide
topLevel.summary: The step-by-step usage guide (this map indexes its chapters).

topLevel.title: Module manifest contract
topLevel.summary: The damat.json contract, capability ownership, registry refs, and trust model.

topLevel.title: AI contributor guide
topLevel.summary: Repo map, conventions, and common-task recipes for AI assistants.

chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.summary: Understand Damat's core idea: modular, TypeScript-first backends built from reusable domain blades.

chapters.title: Concepts and architecture
chapters.summary: Build the mental model for modules, durable work, PostgreSQL truth, Redis acceleration, and runtime role separation.

chapters.title: Module boundaries and portability
chapters.summary: Separate module-owned behavior from host-owned composition and lifecycle policy.

chapters.title: Execution primitives
chapters.summary: Choose among route, workflow, job, event, and pipeline based on durability and restart needs.

chapters.title: Composition and durability runtime
chapters.summary: Split durable truth from acceleration, and understand runtime modes and migrations.

chapters.title: Getting started
chapters.summary: Create your first app quickly, provision PostgreSQL, understand generated structure, and run your first endpoint.

chapters.title: Prerequisites and local run
chapters.summary: Provision local PostgreSQL, optional Redis, and run the initial CLI and app startup flow.

chapters.title: Project structure walkthrough
chapters.summary: Understand how app contracts, module folders, and durable artifacts are organized.

chapters.title: Configuration & environment
chapters.summary: Learn which knobs control modules, environment loading, worker selection, and policy settings in `damat.config.ts`.

chapters.title: Configuration sections
chapters.summary: Map `projectConfig`, `services`, `modules`, and `providers` to ownership and responsibilities.

chapters.title: Environment loading and variables
chapters.summary: Understand env precedence, required variables, and module env declarations.

chapters.title: Choosing a runtime role
chapters.summary: Choose server, worker, or combined runtime, and understand worker role behavior under restart.

chapters.title: Startup behavior and safety
chapters.summary: Learn `runtime.mode`, worker roles, Redis fallback, and startup migration checks.

chapters.title: Defining models (the ORM DSL)
chapters.summary: Compose typed PostgreSQL schemas with fluent columns, relations, indexes, constraints, and migrations-ready model metadata.

chapters.title: Model columns and types
chapters.summary: Use column builders and modifiers to define stable types and defaults without ad-hoc SQL.

chapters.title: Relations, indexes, and constraints
chapters.summary: Use module-local relations and constraints, then isolate cross-module links in app-owned link modules.

chapters.title: Migrations
chapters.summary: Plan schema changes safely across modules with generated snapshot diffs and shared durability/system migrations.

chapters.title: App migration workflow
chapters.summary: Run host-owned migration setup, checks, and status commands for safe startup and deploy flow.

chapters.title: Standalone module migration workflow
chapters.summary: Use module migration commands in local module context and keep ownership boundaries intact.

chapters.title: Modules & services
chapters.summary: Turn model definitions into typed domain services, typed credentials, and module entrypoints.

chapters.title: Querying & the CRUD service
chapters.summary: Use generated find/write APIs, where-operators, transactions, and optional read-cache/event/logging features.

chapters.title: Querying options and filters
chapters.summary: Master paging, filtering, sorting, and projection for generated service queries.

chapters.title: Transactions and consistency
chapters.summary: Understand transaction scopes, validation, caching, events, and query logging.

chapters.title: Building HTTP APIs
chapters.summary: Design file-based route trees with Hono, typed handlers, validation, and predictable response conventions.

chapters.title: HTTP validation and composition
chapters.summary: Split request validation and route middleware into predictable handler files.

chapters.title: Authentication
chapters.summary: Attach an auth provider, shape request principals, and secure routes with session/API-key based access.

chapters.title: Authentication implementation
chapters.summary: Implement the auth role using provider contracts and explicit route-level enforcement.

chapters.title: Integration providers
chapters.summary: Adopt provider role contracts (auth/payment/subscription) and expose clean integration seams from modules.

chapters.title: Provider implementation and integration
chapters.summary: Implement payment and subscription-like providers with typed role methods and explicit module binding.

chapters.title: Workflows (the saga engine)
chapters.summary: Orchestrate local, compensable business steps with retries and timeouts while one process remains alive.

chapters.title: Implement a workflow
chapters.summary: Build typed steps, compensation payloads, and a composed in-process saga.

chapters.title: Workflow reliability and errors
chapters.summary: Tune retries, timeouts, lock scope, and failure interpretation.

chapters.title: Redis acceleration and utilities
chapters.summary: Add optional acceleration for cache, liveness, pub/sub, locks, sessions, and rate limiting without changing durability semantics.

chapters.title: Cache and rate limits
chapters.summary: Use typed cache helpers, tag-based invalidation, and Redis-based per-identity request limits.

chapters.title: Locks, queues, and sessions
chapters.summary: Protect critical sections and ephemeral queue patterns while keeping jobs/events durable in PostgreSQL.

chapters.title: Events and background jobs
chapters.summary: Build retryable async work and per-consumer event delivery with PostgreSQL-first persistence and observability.

chapters.title: Define jobs and durable events
chapters.summary: Define durable jobs/events, enable capabilities, and wire request-level transaction context.

chapters.title: Publish durable work atomically
chapters.summary: Queue jobs and publish durable events with transaction alignment and idempotency metadata.

chapters.title: Inspect and recover durable work
chapters.summary: Inspect failed work, retry safely, and understand operational semantics under Redis fallback.

chapters.title: Durable pipelines
chapters.summary: Persisted orchestration for restart-safe process flows with waits, branches, signals, and durable stage state.

chapters.title: Define a pipeline
chapters.summary: Design node graphs with typed payload wiring, branches, loops, child pipelines, and resilient start/signal flows.

chapters.title: Start and signal a pipeline run
chapters.summary: Start pipeline runs and send durable signals with actor, reason, and idempotency context.

chapters.title: Configure and operate pipelines
chapters.summary: Configure workers, signals, migration readiness, retention, and production-safe fallback behavior.

chapters.title: Logging
chapters.summary: Tune structured logs and outputs for local debugging, production diagnostics, and operational diagnostics.

chapters.title: The default backend, end to end
chapters.summary: Follow the reference app end-to-end to map every subsystem to a real project structure.

chapters.title: Authoring a module
chapters.summary: Design a single-purpose module with models, config, migrations, tests, and install-ready contracts.

chapters.title: Module service and layering
chapters.summary: Keep service boundaries strict from route to generated accessor, and stay portable.

chapters.title: Test and prepare a module
chapters.summary: Validate module behavior, publish safely, and keep install notes accurate.

chapters.title: Installing existing modules
chapters.summary: Learn module installation workflows across registry refs, local paths, and git sources.

chapters.title: Plan and integrate an install
chapters.summary: Plan install targets, run module plan/add flows, and wire host-owned capabilities manually.

chapters.title: Source, package, and lifecycle
chapters.summary: Use package mode safely, review trust metadata, and update/remove modules cleanly.

chapters.title: Publish modules to a registry
chapters.summary: Publish modules safely with verification, release metadata, and optional self-hosted registries.

chapters.title: Installing modules with AI (MCP)
chapters.summary: Use the MCP server to discover, inspect, and install modules with reduced command context.

chapters.title: Module capabilities
chapters.summary: Understand the full capability surface: schema generation, migrations, workflows, orchestration, tests, and packaging.

chapters.title: Durable module capabilities
chapters.summary: Map module capability families and choose stable boundaries for jobs, events, and pipelines.

chapters.title: Installation and runtime ownership
chapters.summary: Align installer intent, transaction context, and runtime policy with host-owned behavior.

chapters.title: Composing & linking modules
chapters.summary: Compose a backend from independent modules using links, `getModule`, registration, and explicit wiring.

chapters.title: Design an app-owned link
chapters.summary: Define app-owned cross-module relations with explicit link endpoints and ownership.

chapters.title: Activate and query links
chapters.summary: Run migrations, query linked graph fields, and manage dormant shipped links safely.

chapters.title: CLI reference
chapters.summary: Find exact commands for backend workflows: create, migrate, dev loops, install, build, and inspect.

chapters.title: Deployment
chapters.summary: Deploy confidently with explicit migration jobs, stable runtime roles, and process-mode guardrails.

chapters.title: Containers, health, and rollback
chapters.summary: Split deployment into release, container, and rollback safety paths.

chapters.title: Package reference
chapters.summary: Jump straight to package APIs and internal docs from the same navigation tree as the guide.

chapters.title: Troubleshooting
chapters.summary: Resolve startup, runtime, migration, and durability issues quickly with symptom-first checklists.

chapters.title: Runtime and durability faults
chapters.summary: Diagnose pipeline, jobs, events, Redis, and startup signal issues.

chapters.title: Tooling and build faults
chapters.summary: Resolve module, MCP, and toolchain issues with command-first diagnostics.
